newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Kremlin confirms Yeltsin offer to liberal Nemtsov.
newsitem.headline: Kremlin confirms Yeltsin offer to liberal Nemtsov.

text.p: A Kremlin spokesman confirmed on Monday that President Boris Yeltsin had offered to make the liberal governor of the Nizhny Novgorod region, Boris Nemtsov, first deputy prime minister in the new Russian government.
The spokesman could not confirm a report by Interfax news agency that Nemtsov had accepted the offer which would make him equal to reformer Anatoly Chubais who already holds the same position.
Interfax quoted sources as saying Nemtsov, 37, would be in charge of natural monopolies, the social sphere and relations with regional authorities.
There is a very interesting variant," Interfax quoted Yeltsin as telling Nemtsov. "Two young men -- you and Anatoly Chubais -- create a fresh young team in the government, from scratch.
"No one (else) has been appointed yet. All candidates to the government will be agreed with the two first deputy premiers."
Yeltsin was due to meet Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and Chubais later on Tuesday to discuss the government reshuffle ordered by the Kremlin leader.
